analyst_note: FIRE-SALES OBSERVABILITY HOLES CLOSED FROM PRIMARY FILINGS — one channel ruled out, two obligations found worse than recorded. Rating unchanged at AMBER, but its basis is no longer "unquantified null". (1) INSIDER PLEDGES ARE IMMATERIAL. The merger agreement was the wrong document — it contains no margin, collateral or pledge provisions at all ("pledge" appears once, inside the boilerplate Lien definition). The disclosure lives in the 424B4 beneficial-ownership footnotes: Musk 237,530 Class A and Nosek 2,381,000 Class A "pledged as security for personal indebtedness", 2,618,530 shares total, ~$300.9M at the $114.92 close. That is 0.0199% of the 13,181,779,945 shares outstanding (10-Q cover, as of 07-28, which also filing-confirms the ~13.18B carried since 08-06), 0.168% of post-unlock float, and ~1.07% of the 08-06 session's 245M volume. Total foreclosure on every disclosed pledge is about one percent of one day's trading, so pledge-driven forced selling cannot produce a fire sale at any price. Two structural reasons the figure is so small: Class B auto-converts to Class A on any pledge or hypothecation, so the supervoting holders are penalised for pledging; and the pledges that exist are individually small (Musk's is 0.028% of his ~849.5M Class A; Nosek's is 7.22% of his 32.99M). Cutting the other way, lock-up exception (xv) lets a third-party pledgee enforce its security interest by SELLING lock-up securities — pledged shares do escape the lockup on foreclosure — but that transmission channel is bounded by the same 2.6M shares. (2) THE CURSOR CONSIDERATION HAS NO COLLAR, now verified rather than inferred. "VWAP" never appears in the agreement; the defined term is Parent Share Price = the volume-weighted average closing price over the seven consecutive trading days ending the trading day immediately preceding Closing. Exchange Ratio = Company Implied Per Share Value / Parent Share Price, where Company Implied Per Share Value divides a FIXED $60,000,000,000 equity value by Anysphere's fully diluted capitalisation. Section 2.05 Adjustments covers only reclassifications, splits, recaps and stock dividends — nothing price-contingent. There is no floor, no ceiling and no price-based walk-away, so issuance scales as 1/P without bound: 444.4M shares at the $135 offer, 522.1M at the $114.92 close (+77.7M, +17.5%), 570.8M at the $105.11 all-time low, 666.7M at $90, 800.0M at $75 — 3.37% / 3.96% / 4.33% / 5.06% / 6.07% of shares outstanding respectively. Each 10% decline issues 11.1% more stock. Those shares carry a Lock-Up Period per the Letter of Transmittal and Exhibit D, so they do not hit float at closing. (3) THE TERMINATION FEE BECAME CASH-ONLY WHEN SPCX LISTED. Section 11.04(d): a Private Parent may elect cash or Termination Shares, but "if Parent is a Public Parent, such fee shall be payable only in cash in immediately available funds". SPCX listed 06-12, so the stock-settlement escape hatch is closed — $10B Total Fee or $4B Regulatory Total Fee, in cash, and Section 11.04(e) confirms never both. A contingent obligation previously readable as stock-settled is a hard cash claim, crystallising precisely when stock is the weaker currency. Also newly visible: the $10B fee is conditioned on a separate SPCX-Anysphere COMPUTE AGREEMENT (payable only if Parent has not terminated, and is not entitled to terminate, that agreement for a "Specified Material Breach") — a counterparty-web node not previously tracked. Company-level secured debt is asset-backed, not stock-backed: a $1.5B ABL revolver against inventory and equipment, equipment financings at ~5.3-5.5%, and a facility collateralised by securities held in xAI's custodial account. NET: the pledge channel is ruled out (de-escalating), the obligation structure is confirmed worse than recorded (holding). AMBER is unchanged and now specified rather than merely unresolved.

runs.driving_observable: HELD AT AMBER — de-escalation candidate, not yet de-escalated. The armed catalyst fired and did NOT produce the RED marker: the compound test was a turnover spike ON FALLING price, and the session delivered a turnover spike on RISING price (2.0-2.1x average volume, close +6.14%). The 'break below the recent ~$108-111 lows on elevated volume' clause was touched intraday ($105.11, a new all-time low) but reversed within the session to close near the high — a supply test met by demand, which is the opposite of a run. Two reasons this is not yet GREEN. (1) The de-escalation clause requires 'modest REALIZED selling', and realized selling is unobservable today: Form 4s lag up to two business days, so no insider-disposition data exists yet for 08-06. Absent that, a GREEN call would rest on price action alone. (2) The structural run capacity rose sharply — free float went 4.9% -> 11.8% of shares outstanding — and only the first 20% tranche is out, with further staggered tranches through the 2026-12-08 full expiry. The mechanism is better-capitalized against a run than yesterday in sentiment terms and materially worse in structural terms.

fire_sales.driving_observable: HELD AT AMBER — unchanged rating, materially better-specified basis. The AMBER condition is untouched: price remains below the $135 offer, so stock-settled obligations are not covered with headroom. What changed is that the two "unquantified null" holes flagged since 08-05 have been worked from primary filings, and they resolve in opposite directions. The PLEDGE channel is now ruled out: only 2,618,530 Class A shares are disclosed as pledged for personal indebtedness (Musk 237,530, Nosek 2,381,000) = 0.0199% of shares outstanding, 0.168% of float, ~1% of one session's volume. Private loan trigger LEVELS are still undisclosed and always will be — they live in unfiled agreements — but that no longer gates the rating, because the maximum supply from total foreclosure is immaterial at any trigger price. The OBLIGATION structure is confirmed worse than recorded: the Cursor consideration is a fixed $60B of value divided by a 7-day VWAP with NO COLLAR (Section 2.05 adjusts only for recapitalisation events), so dilution scales as 1/P without bound — 522.1M shares at the $114.92 close versus 444.4M at the offer, and 800.0M at $75; and the $10B / $4B termination fees became payable ONLY IN CASH once SPCX became a Public Parent (Section 11.04(d)), removing the stock-settlement election a private issuer would have had. No forced event is visible: no margin call, no pledged-share liquidation, no renegotiation or collapse. RED still requires a visible forced event, and the pledge finding makes one materially less likely from that channel.

fire_sales.next_escalation_trigger: Re-rate to RED on a visible forced event: renegotiation or collapse of the Cursor deal crystallising the $10B/$4B CASH termination exposure, or a slide deep enough to materially reprice the uncollared issuance. Pledged-share liquidation is DOWNGRADED as a RED pathway — at 2.6M shares disclosed it cannot move the tape, and it should not be treated as a live escalation route unless a new pledge appears in a later filing. The Q3 closing date remains the scheduled resolution point, and the specific interval to watch is the 7 consecutive trading days ending the day before Closing, which mechanically fixes the issuance count. NEW WATCH ITEMS, both press-independent: (a) any increase in disclosed pledges in a subsequent 10-Q, proxy or Form 4/144, which would reopen a channel now closed; (b) the SPCX-Anysphere Compute Agreement, which conditions the $10B fee and is not otherwise tracked.
